findings.title: DPDP §3 — Applicability
findings.message: Digital personal data processing detected. Verify whether data principals are located in India or services target individuals in India.

findings.title: DPDP §5 — Notice Requirements
findings.message: Verify that consent requests present an itemised notice detailing data fields, purpose, withdrawal under §6(4), Data Principal rights (§§11–14), and Board grievance procedures.

findings.title: DPDP §6(9) — Consent Manager Registration
findings.message: Consent Managers used to manage Data Principal consent must be registered with the Data Protection Board. (Tier 2 requirement effective 13 Nov 2026).

findings.title: DPDP §8(3) — Accuracy and Completeness
findings.message: Verify that personal data used to make decisions affecting individuals or shared onward is accurate, complete, and consistent.

findings.title: DPDP §8(6) — Personal Data Breach Notification
findings.message: Verify technical logging, alerting, and incident response readiness to notify BOTH the Data Protection Board and ALL affected Data Principals in the event of a personal data breach. Note: DPDP §8(6) does not contain a GDPR-style high-risk severity gate.

findings.title: DPDP §8(9) — Designated Contact / Privacy Information
findings.message: Designated contact / applicable DPO information could not be technically established from repository evidence under DPDP §8(9).

findings.title: DPDP §8(10) — Grievance Redressal Mechanism
findings.message: Data Fiduciaries must provide an easily accessible grievance submission mechanism for Data Principals.

findings.title: DPDP §9 — Processing of Children's & Disabled Persons' Data
findings.message: DPDP §9 establishes a distinct children's data regime requiring verifiable parental consent before processing data of minors (<18), prohibiting harmful processing, and banning behavioral tracking or targeted advertising.

findings.title: DPDP §10 — Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF) Obligations
findings.message: SDF applicability is a government notification threshold based on processing volume, sensitivity, and risk. Scanner cannot auto-determine SDF status.

findings.title: DPDP §14 — Right to Nominate
findings.message: DPDP §14 grants Data Principals the right to nominate an individual to exercise rights on their death/incapacity. (DPDP-specific requirement with no direct GDPR analog).

findings.title: DPDP §16 — Cross-Border Data Transfer
findings.message: No countries are currently configured as restricted under DPDP §16; restriction-based cross-border findings are not being generated from this dataset.

findings.title: CRA Vulnerability Disclosure Policy & Contact (SECURITY.md)
findings.message: No SECURITY.md file detected. CRA Annex I Part II (CRA-II-4, CRA-II-5, CRA-II-6) requires a vulnerability disclosure policy, reporting contact, and advisory process. (Shared with CERT-In security contact requirement).

findings.title: CRA-I-3h Vulnerability Update Delivery Mechanism
findings.message: No automated release or container publishing workflow identified in repository context.

findings.title: CRA-I-3e Availability & DoS Resilience Checklist
findings.message: Availability & DoS resilience testing cannot be established from application source code alone. Organizational attestation and test documentation required.

findings.title: CRA-II-7 Free Security Patch Distribution Checklist
findings.message: Organizational policy must ensure security updates are provided to end users free of charge and accompanied by advisory information.

findings.title: CRA-II-8 ENISA/CSIRT 24-Hour Reporting Checklist
findings.message: Process and named incident owner must exist to notify ENISA and designated CSIRT within 24 hours of becoming aware of actively exploited vulnerabilities.

findings.title: CERT-In §5(v) Log Retention (180 Days) & Data Residency
findings.message: Repository configuration evidence detected (Indian cloud region reference ('ap-south-1') and 180-day log retention setting in 'src/compliance/cert_in_engine.py'). Note: Configuration is evidence of configured retention/residency, NOT proof that production CERT-In logs are actually retained for 180 days or stored in India.
